extracted.intended_audience: Principal investigators and research teams preparing or reviewing NSF proposals (NSF proposal writers and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating NSF research proposals using the two official Merit Review Criteria (Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts) and the five elements reviewers must consider for each criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Intellectual Merit criterion assesses the potential for the proposed project to advance knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of the two NSF Merit Review Criteria. Reviewers evaluate how the project will contribute to knowledge and understanding. The five Elements (listed separately) are to be applied when assessing Intellectual Merit (e.g., whether the project will advance knowledge; whether it is creative or transformative; whether the plan is well-reasoned and includes assessment; the qualifications of the investigators; and availability of resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Broader Impacts criterion assesses the potential for the proposed project to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the second NSF Merit Review Criterion. Reviewers evaluate how the project could produce societal benefits or advance desired outcomes. The five Elements (listed separately) are to be applied when assessing Broader Impacts (e.g., what societal benefits are expected; whether activities are creative or transformative in achieving impacts; whether there is an assessment mechanism; investigator capacity to achieve broader impacts; and available resources/support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to advance knowledge or benefit society
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the potential for the proposed activity to: (Intellectual Merit) Advance knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields? (Broader Impacts) Benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explicitly consider the degree and nature of expected advances or benefits. For Intellectual Merit, focus on advancement of knowledge/understanding; for Broader Impacts, focus on tangible or anticipated societal outcomes. This element frames the core substantive contribution for each criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity, originality, and transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty and whether the project challenges existing paradigms or could lead to significant shifts in the field or in practice. Applies to both Intellectual Merit (novel research ideas) and Broader Impacts (innovative approaches to achieving societal outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of plan and assessment mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the plan for carrying out the proposed activities well-reasoned, well-organized, and based on a sound rationale? Does the plan incorporate a mechanism to assess success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity, organization, feasibility, logical rationale, and whether appropriate milestones, metrics, or evaluation methods are included to judge progress and outcomes. This includes methodological rigor for research and concrete plans to measure broader impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of individuals, team, or organization
rubrics_metrics.description: How well qualified is the individual, team, or organization to conduct the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider prior accomplishments, expertise, complementary skills among team members, institutional support, and track record relevant to both executing the research (Intellectual Merit) and achieving broader impacts. Assess whether the project team has the capacity to deliver the proposed outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there adequate resources available to the PI (either at the home organization or through collaborations) to carry out the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review institutional facilities, equipment, collaborators, and other support (financial, administrative, partnerships) that enable successful execution. Determine whether available resources are sufficient to realize both the research objectives and the broader impact plans.
